Independent first source audit of RFC4271-4.4-1. RFC4271 Section4.4 states: "KEEPALIVE messages MUST NOT be sent more frequently than one per second." Read that whole section, Section4.2 legal negotiated HoldTime and Section10 automatic one-third interval/jitter context, both complete current tagged units and their real producer/clock/cleanup helpers, owning FSM pages and actual Session send coupling. The one-third interval and recommended jitter do not waive the one-second minimum. The current official RFC Editor update list and verified-errata inline rendering preserve this rate sentence; the local RFC9687 SendHoldTimer changes do not relax it. No local RFC4271 errata file is present and the separate RFC Editor errata-search endpoint was unavailable, so no exhaustive claim about every reported erratum is made. RFC text, not an informative inline rendering or our summary, remains the requirement authority.
The assessed baseline is the default zero/automatic KeepaliveTime, with the timer supplied legal minimum negotiated HoldTime3s. This is a timer callback observation, not a test of OPEN negotiation or Session/TCP delivery. The positive sets only its new object's random draw to0 before arming, representing the permitted minimum jitter: base1s becomes750ms before the floor. It asserts a running timer, counts0 at999ms,1 at1s,1 at1.999s and2 at2s, so suppressing all callbacks cannot satisfy it. The original running/count assertions are intact and cleanup stops the chain. The negative independently samples HoldTime3/30/90: no callback at999ms and exactly one by hold/3; zero HoldTime produces no callback after one hour. These are the actual sampled initial-arm/zero controls, not an exhaustive execution of every hold value, configured override, concurrency schedule or periodic rearm. Its larger values and zero distinguish bounded scope conditions from the positive shortest-interval repeat witness.

This is a normal-return semantic rate fault, not a panic, getter-copy or timeout witness. Main supplied a separate three-root race package PASS37853,1.218s; its nonverbose package output is not substituted for named-unit evidence. Only this positive selective record has been read; the negative has no recorded discrimination, and no all-cover-record completion is claimed. Main still owes its final native freshness and scoped lint before stamping/publication.
Source coupling supports the default rate obligation without claiming an observed wire test: NewSession installs the real timer callback, which synchronously emits the keepalive FSM event and calls sendKeepalive when connected; sendKeepalive emits one KEEPALIVE through the ordinary synchronous control writer. StartKeepaliveTimer applies max1s to both initial and repeat arms, and rearms only after the callback returns, so a slow send cannot shorten the next repeat. NewPeerSettings leaves KeepaliveTime0 and default receive hold90; publishNegotiation supplies the smaller legal peer hold, allowing3s. The ordinary non-delayed/non-BFD OPEN branch sends its initial KEEPALIVE while holding OPEN admission serialization; handleKeepalive starts the timer once on OpenConfirm entry to Established, and steady-state incoming KEEPALIVEs do not restart it. The direct tagged timer tests do not execute these Session paths: their role here is read, bound production coupling, not an invented OPEN, foreign-peer, TCP/kernel timestamp, restart-race or optional BFD/DelayOpen observation. Explicit operator timing and other extension features remain supported under the standing baseline-versus-option rule; no structural FSM rewrite or feature removal is required or inferred.
Enforced is the independent source-and-assertion judgment for this default rate obligation, with the precise callback transport and recorded-cover limits above; it is not a claim that every tagged cover has a fresh record or that the full RFC goal is complete. This first pending input has no computed fingerprints. It may be natively stamped against the qualified working source after main's checks; if source=head is chosen, first publish the applied test and accepted record coherently, then stamp that committed source. No working-tree stamping prohibition is invented.
